content: Nutmeg oil is a volatile essential oil that contains borneol and eugenol. It is extracted through the process of steam distillation from ground nutmeg. This oil is widely utilized in the perfumery and pharmaceutical industries. It is either colorless or light yellow in appearance and has the characteristic aroma and taste of nutmeg. In the food industry, nutmeg oil is often used as a substitute for ground nutmeg because it does not leave any particles in the food. It is also a common ingredient in beverages, sweets, and products like Coca-Cola. Additionally, nutmeg oil is employed in the cosmetic and pharmaceutical sectors, such as in toothpaste formulations and as a key component in certain cough syrups. Historically, nutmeg and its oil have been used in traditional medicine to address conditions affecting the nervous and digestive systems. The compound myristicin, present in nutmeg oil, is believed to be responsible for its hallucinogenic properties. Externally, nutmeg oil is applied to alleviate rheumatic pain. Similar to clove oil, it can be used as an emergency remedy for toothache. In such cases, a small amount of the oil can be applied to the gums around the affected tooth using a cotton swab until professional dental care is available. In France, nutmeg oil is administered in drop doses mixed with honey to treat digestive disturbances and bad breath. For nausea, gastroenteritis, chronic diarrhea, and indigestion, 3 to 5 drops of nutmeg oil can be taken on a sugar lump or mixed into a teaspoon of honey. Alternatively, a massage oil can be prepared by diluting 10 drops of nutmeg oil in 10 milliliters of almond oil. This mixture is effective for relieving muscular pain associated with rheumatism or physical overexertion. It can also be combined with other essential oils, such as thyme or rosemary, for enhanced effects. To prepare for childbirth, a massage oil can be created by mixing 5 drops of nutmeg oil and up to 5 drops of sage oil in 25 milliliters of almond oil. This mixture can be massaged onto the abdomen daily during the three weeks leading up to the expected delivery date.
